High water conditions reportedly exist at L/D 1, in the vicinity of Mile 9.1.  Mariners are advised to exercise caution due to the hazardous conditions associated with strong currents, increased drift, increased drafting toward bridge piers and severe outdrafts.  Mariners are advised to consider horsepower capability and tow size.  Fleet operators should regularly check their fleets and immediately report barge breakaways to the U.S. Coast Guard.

Marine Safety Alert 02-24 - Inspections and Compliance Directorate --- DANGEROUS BYCATCH FROM DISCARDED MUNITIONS REMAINS A PRESENT DAY HAZARD --- This Safety Alert is being issued to raise awareness of lurking hazards caused by discarded munitions, which often contain active explosives or chemical agents. Although the practice of dumping munitions into the sea ceased in 1970, a significant amount remains hidden in coastal waters, posing a safety hazard to commercial fisherman, dredge operators, and others who trawl and work the ocean floor. 
Recently, a deckhand on a clamming vessel was severely burned when a canister was dredged up and brought onboard with clams and other debris. The canister likely contained mustard gas or another blistering agent, but did not display any obvious visual, audible, or odor indicators of discharging content. --- U.S. Coast Guard Heartland District Hurricane Season 2026 --- The 2026 Hurricane Season extends from June 1, 2026 through November 30, 2026.  Tropical storms and hurricanes often develop with little warning.  Extensive damage to small craft often results in loss of life.  All mariners, particularly operators of small fishing vessels, are reminded that advanced planning, which may prevent loss of vessel and crew, should include:  
a) Instruction of crew and passengers in location of emergency equipment and emergency procedures.
b) Pre-sailing check of vessel, machinery, and equipment for seaworthiness.
c) Installation of strong ground tackle.
d) Review of storm center evacuation procedures.
e) Knowledge of the nearest hurricane shelter or port of refuge.

Shoaling has been reported in the vicinity of Mile 941.5.  Mariners are urged to exercise caution in the area.

The navigation channel width has been reduced to 580 feet, between approximate Miles 110.5 and 109.5.  Mariners are advised to implement a one-way traffic pattern with no meeting, passing or overtaking. d: Continuing until October 31, 2026, pile driving operations are being conducted at the Sandy Quarry, in the vicinity of Mile 674.0.  Work will be conducted from 7:00 a.m. until 6:00 p.m.  The construction crew will monitor VHF-FM Channels 73 and 74.  Mariners are urged to exercise caution in the area.

t: Facilities, Barriers, Manmade Reefs, Riprap, Jetties/Dikes
d: Continuing until March 31, 2027, Underwater Construction Corporation, dredging and mooring cell repairs are being conducted along the RDB, at the AEP Rockport Power Plant, in the vicinity of Mile 744.8.  Work will be conducted from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m., 7-days a week.  The contractors floating plant will consist of one crane barge and one material barge.  Mariners are requested to transit the area at their slowest safe speed to minimize their wake and proceed with caution.

Continuing until further notice, the Dredge MIDWAY is conducting dredging operations in the vicinity of Mile 785.0.  The Dredge MIDWAY will monitor VHF-FM Channel 13 or 71.  Mariners are urged to transit the area at their slowest safe speed to minimize their wake and proceed with caution after passing arrangements have been made.
